article_title.ru: Прогноз формы шнура и выбор движения дали разные результаты
article_title.en: Cable prediction and action selection favor different information
article_title.ja: ひもの形の予測と動作選択を別々に評価

caption.ru: Проверка формы после движения: инженер сверяет изгиб шнура с прямой планкой, коллега записывает результат. Редакционная интерпретация исследования Болонского университета о различии между прогнозом деформации и выбором действия. Люди, робот и способ наглядной проверки обобщены: это не реконструкция установки и не портреты авторов. Исследование ограничено шнуром на плоскости.
caption.en: Checking the shape after a movement: an engineer compares a cable bend with a straight strip while a colleague records the result. An editorial interpretation of the University of Bologna study separating deformation prediction from action selection. People, robot and visual checking method are generalized, not a reconstruction of the apparatus or portraits of the authors. The study is limited to planar cable shaping.
caption.ja: 動作後の形を確かめる。女性技術者が直線の板を目安にひもの曲がりを確認し、同僚が結果を記録する。変形の予測と動作選択を分けて評価したボローニャ大学の研究を題材にした編集イラスト。人物、ロボット、確認方法は一般化した表現で、装置の再現や著者の肖像ではない。研究の対象は平面上のひもの操作に限られる。

alt.ru: Чёрно-белая гравюра: на прочном рабочем столе лежит один шнур с плавным изгибом и двумя видимыми концами. Слева женщина-инженер держит прямую планку на столе и указывает на изгиб шнура. За столом инженер в очках и свитере пишет карандашом на листе, придерживая его другой рукой. Справа закреплена шарнирная роботизированная рука с открытым пустым захватом, отведённым от шнура. Фон белый, надписей и экранов нет.
alt.en: Black-and-white engraving: a single smoothly curved cable with two visible ends rests on a sturdy workbench. At left, a woman engineer holds a straight strip flat on the table and points toward the cable bend. Behind the bench, an engineer in glasses and a sweater writes with a pencil on a sheet steadied by his other hand. At right, an articulated robot arm is fixed to the bench, its empty open gripper parked away from the cable. White background, no lettering or screens.
alt.ja: 白黒の版画。丈夫な作業台の上に、両端が見える一本のひもが緩く曲がって置かれている。左の女性技術者は台上の直線の板を押さえ、ひもの曲がりを指で示す。奥では眼鏡とセーター姿の男性技術者が用紙を片手で押さえ、鉛筆で記録する。右の関節式ロボットアームは台に固定され、空のつかみ部を開いてひもから離している。背景は白く、文字や画面はない。

visual_thesis: Качество прогноза деформации и точность получившейся формы — разные результаты. Иллюстрация сосредоточена на проверке реального результата после действия робота на плоскости. Прямая планка служит наглядным редакционным приёмом, а не утверждением о применявшемся в исследовании измерительном приборе. Сцена не изображает завязывание узлов, промышленный монтаж или доказанное обобщение на другие задачи.
visual_brief:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: exactly ONE original landscape 16:9 editorial newspaper engraving, high quality.

Single article only: University of Bologna researchers studied planar cable shaping. A robot selects a single grasp location and a planar motion; prediction accuracy and the accuracy of the shape actually produced are different evaluations. The physical trials followed simulation-only training. The study is limited to planar cable shaping; it is not knot tying, wiring installation, or autonomous industrial deployment.

Make an explicitly generalized editorial laboratory scene, NOT a photographic reconstruction, NOT an identifiable portrait, NOT an exact product depiction. Do not invent recognizable robot models, university branding, numerical outcomes or apparatus specifications. The visible thesis: examine the cable shape that was actually produced, rather than admire a prediction. Do not include any second story or any screens.

Style: black ink on pure clean WHITE background, mid-twentieth-century Soviet popular-science editorial engraving, modern robotics in a historical graphic language. Strong confident outlines, expressive solid black areas, disciplined moderately spaced hatching and crosshatching, clear silhouettes, ample empty white. Realistic harmonious attractive people with light expressive faces and hands, calm dignity and concentrated technical work. No colour, sepia, toned paper, gouache, neon, decorative borders, political symbols, logos, text, letters, numbers, watermark, pseudo-interface or decorative graphics.

Composition: one substantial uncluttered laboratory workbench in three-quarter view from moderately above, its top and solid supports clearly visible. On the top lies ONE thick flexible cable in a broad uncomplicated S curve, with both cut ends visible, no loops, knots, fittings or connectors. Every part of the cable rests on the tabletop with a small contact shadow; it is not a power cable for any machine, neither end enters a robot or human tool. The cable is the main visual focus.
At the far right of the workbench, one simple generalized articulated robot arm has a firmly attached base, two visibly connected main links and a wrist with a modest opposed parallel-jaw gripper. The arm has finished an action and is parked safely to the side. Its two jaws are OPEN and EMPTY, clearly separated above an empty area of the table, NOT holding the cable, NOT touching the people, nothing dangling from the wrist. Do not show multiple arms or ghost poses. Simple mechanically credible geometry, no gratuitous protrusions, handles or cables. Do not imply that a device on screen controls a physical object: there are no screens.

Exactly TWO adult colleagues, at a natural professional working distance, both actively working:
1. A woman engineer about thirty-five, tied-back hair, pleasant focused face, light practical technical work jacket with sleeves kept clear, trousers. At the left/front of the bench she checks the cable's resulting shape with a plain straight measuring strip laid flat on an empty patch of the tabletop beside the cable. Her left hand holds the strip flat at one end; her right index finger points to a nearby bend of the cable without touching it. The rigid strip does not cross, pass underneath, or penetrate the cable; both are supported by the same flat tabletop. Her eyes are on the cable bend and strip. The strip has no readable graduations, numbers, or lettering. This is a generalized visual metaphor of checking the result, not a claim about the paper's actual measurement apparatus.
2. A male engineer about thirty, short tidy hair, clean-shaven, simple eyeglasses and a plain knitted crewneck sweater. At the opposite end to her, well outside the parked robot's workspace, he writes results with a pencil on ONE plain sheet lying flat on the bench. Pencil tip visibly contacts the paper; his other hand steadies the paper. His eyes follow the page while recording, natural posture, no posing. No readable writing on the page.

The woman is measuring/checking the robot-shaped cable; the man is recording findings. Both actions should be evident without a caption. Do not add romantic glances, touching between colleagues, chin-on-hand poses, fashion posing, lab coats used as costume, irrelevant goggles, extra tools, coffee cups, posters, architectural clutter or background machinery. Keep faces/hands light and readable. All hands anatomically plausible. Every significant object must have a visible support and every tool an intelligible contact: pencil to paper, hand to strip, strip to table, cable to table, robot base to bench. No floating objects, intersecting solids, detached mechanisms or implausible grasps. Keep the critical cable/table contact and two human work actions legible even when reduced for black-and-white print. One coherent calm scene; no collage, insets, charts, comparison panels or explanatory overlays.
